description: 0/0 at a finite point involving a square root: multiply by the conjugate to rationalize, then cancel and substitute.

exercises.technique: 0/0 at x=2. Factor numerator x^3-8=(x-2)(x^2+2x+4); rationalize the denominator by multiplying by (sqrt(x+2)+2), which turns sqrt(x+2)-2 into (x-2)/(sqrt(x+2)+2). The (x-2) factors cancel, leaving (x^2+2x+4)(sqrt(x+2)+2).
0/0 at x=3. Rationalize the numerator (multiply by sqrt(x+6)+3) to get (x-3)/(sqrt(x+6)+3); factor denominator x^3-27=(x-3)(x^2+3x+9). Cancel (x-3), leaving 1/[(sqrt(x+6)+3)(x^2+3x+9)].
0/0 at x=1. Rationalize both numerator and denominator by multiplying by (sqrt(x+3)+2) and (sqrt(x)+1); this turns the ratio into (x-1)(sqrt x+1) / [(x-1)(sqrt(x+3)+2)], and the (x-1) factors cancel.
0/0 at x=3. Factor numerator x^3-27=(x-3)(x^2+3x+9); rationalize denominator sqrt(x+6)-3=(x-3)/(sqrt(x+6)+3). The (x-3) factors cancel, leaving (x^2+3x+9)(sqrt(x+6)+3)/27.

0/0 at x=2. Rationalize the numerator by multiplying by (2+sqrt(x+2)): (4-(x+2))=(2-x), giving -(x-2)/(2+sqrt(x+2)). Factor denominator x^3-8=(x-2)(x^2+2x+4); cancel (x-2), leaving -1/[(2+sqrt(x+2))(x^2+2x+4)].
